claim: The claustrum has been implicated in attention.
source: The claustrum has been implicated in a variety of functions and behaviors, including attention (Atlan et al., 2018; Goll et al., 2015; Smith et al., 2019), impulsivity (Liu et al., 2019), sleep (Narikiyo et al., 2020; Norimoto et al., 2020; Renouard et al., 2015), and the integration of information to support consciousness (Crick and Koch, 2005; Smythies et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to Atlan et al., 2018; Goll et al., 2015; Smith et al., 2019

claim: The claustrum has been implicated in impulsivity.
source: The claustrum has been implicated in a variety of functions and behaviors, including attention (Atlan et al., 2018; Goll et al., 2015; Smith et al., 2019), impulsivity (Liu et al., 2019), sleep (Narikiyo et al., 2020; Norimoto et al., 2020; Renouard et al., 2015), and the integration of information to support consciousness (Crick and Koch, 2005; Smythies et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Liu et al., 2019

claim: The claustrum has been implicated in sleep.
source: The claustrum has been implicated in a variety of functions and behaviors, including attention (Atlan et al., 2018; Goll et al., 2015; Smith et al., 2019), impulsivity (Liu et al., 2019), sleep (Narikiyo et al., 2020; Norimoto et al., 2020; Renouard et al., 2015), and the integration of information to support consciousness (Crick and Koch, 2005; Smythies et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to Narikiyo et al., 2020; Norimoto et al., 2020; Renouard et al., 2015

claim: The claustrum has been implicated in the integration of information to support consciousness.
source: The claustrum has been implicated in a variety of functions and behaviors, including attention (Atlan et al., 2018; Goll et al., 2015; Smith et al., 2019), impulsivity (Liu et al., 2019), sleep (Narikiyo et al., 2020; Norimoto et al., 2020; Renouard et al., 2015), and the integration of information to support consciousness (Crick and Koch, 2005; Smythies et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to Crick and Koch, 2005; Smythies et al., 2012

claim: The precise anatomical boundaries of the claustrum are a matter of debate.
source: However, such an interpretation is challenged by the fact that even the precise anatomical boundaries of the claustrum are a matter of debate (Dillingham et al., 2019; Smith et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to Dillingham et al., 2019; Smith et al., 2019

claim: Single-cell RNA sequencing identified two discrete populations of excitatory claustral neurons.
source: Beginning with single-cell RNA sequencing, we identified two discrete populations of excitatory claustral neurons.
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq data presented in the manuscript

claim: Multiplexed single-molecule fluorescent in situ hybridization revealed core and shell claustral neuron subtypes.
source: To map the topography of these populations, we used multiplexed single-molecule fluorescent in situ hybridization, revealing core and shell claustral neuron subtypes that were transcriptionally distinguishable relative to surrounding cortical neurons.
evidence: Supported by mFISH data presented in the manuscript

claim: Core and shell claustral neuron subtypes are transcriptionally distinguishable relative to surrounding cortical neurons.
source: To map the topography of these populations, we used multiplexed single-molecule fluorescent in situ hybridization, revealing core and shell claustral neuron subtypes that were transcriptionally distinguishable relative to surrounding cortical neurons.
evidence: Supported by mFISH and scRNA-seq data showing differential gene expression

claim: Multicolor retrograde tracing revealed a spatial organization of distinct cortical-projecting claustral populations that mapped onto the identified core and shell subtypes.
source: Combining this with multicolor retrograde tracing, we revealed a spatial organization of distinct cortical-projecting claustral populations that mapped onto the identified core and shell subtypes.
evidence: Supported by retrograde tracing data combined with mFISH

claim: The claustrum consists of heterogeneous populations of excitatory neurons that are topographically organized.
source: This work demonstrates that the claustrum consists of heterogeneous populations of excitatory neurons that are topographically organized and project to functionally dissociable cortical regions, suggesting subtype-specific functionality of excitatory claustral neurons.
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq, mFISH, and retrograde tracing data

claim: Claustral excitatory neurons project to functionally dissociable cortical regions.
source: This work demonstrates that the claustrum consists of heterogeneous populations of excitatory neurons that are topographically organized and project to functionally dissociable cortical regions, suggesting subtype-specific functionality of excitatory claustral neurons.
evidence: Supported by retrograde tracing data showing projections to RSC and LEC

claim: 1112 cells were manually harvested based on a combination of unbiased blind selection and selection of specific labeled projections.
source: From claustral microdissections from four mice, we manually harvested 1112 cells based on a combination of unbiased blind selection of cells and selection of specific labeled projections (to either the lateral entorhinal cortex [LEC] or retrosplenial cortex [RSC]; see Materials and methods).
evidence: Describes the experimental procedure for cell collection

claim: After library preparation, sequencing, and filtering, 1011 excitatory neurons were retained for analysis.
source: After library preparation, sequencing, and filtering, we retained a total of 1011 excitatory neurons for analysis (n = 478 cells blindly selected; n = 286 and 247 cells projecting to the LEC and RSC, respectively).
evidence: Describes the data processing and filtering steps

claim: UMAP nonlinear dimensionality reduction combined with Louvain graph-based clustering revealed that cells broadly conformed to three transcriptomically separated clusters.
source: Combining UMAP nonlinear dimensionality reduction (McInnes et al., 2018) with Louvain graph-based clustering (Stuart et al., 2019) revealed that cells broadly conformed to three transcriptomically separated clusters (Figure 1A; also seen in t-SNE: Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by computational analysis and visualization in Figure 1A

claim: All three clusters were associated with expression of excitatory neuronal markers.
source: These clusters were all associated with expression of excitatory neuronal markers (Figure 1B) and were found across the anterior-posterior axis and across animals (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: Supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 1B

claim: The three clusters were found across the anterior-posterior axis and across animals.
source: These clusters were all associated with expression of excitatory neuronal markers (Figure 1B) and were found across the anterior-posterior axis and across animals (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B,C

claim: Cluster 1 was enriched for the claustrum marker gene Synpr.
source: In seeking to assign transcriptomic phenotypes to these cells, we noted one cluster ('Cluster 1') was enriched for the claustrum marker gene Synpr (Binks et al., 2019; Wang et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by gene expression data and citations to Binks et al., 2019; Wang et al., 2017

claim: Cluster 1 and Cluster 2 exhibited enriched expression of claustrum marker genes (e.g., Gnb4) relative to Cluster 3.
source: This cluster and a second cluster ('Cluster 2') exhibited enriched expression of other claustrum marker genes (e.g., Gnb4) relative to the third cluster ('Cluster 3') (Figure 1C), with Cluster 2 also showing uniquely expressed marker genes (e.g., Slc30a3; Figure 1D).
evidence: Supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 1C

claim: Cluster 2 showed uniquely expressed marker genes including Slc30a3.
source: This cluster and a second cluster ('Cluster 2') exhibited enriched expression of other claustrum marker genes (e.g., Gnb4) relative to the third cluster ('Cluster 3') (Figure 1C), with Cluster 2 also showing uniquely expressed marker genes (e.g., Slc30a3; Figure 1D).
evidence: Supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 1D

claim: Cluster 3 was enriched for markers of excitatory cortical populations including the layer 6b marker Ctgf and the layer 6a marker Sla.
source: Conversely, Cluster 3 was enriched for markers of excitatory cortical populations (e.g., the layer 6b marker Ctgf and the layer 6a marker Sla) (Tasic et al., 2016; Tasic et al., 2018), suggesting a cortical phenotype (Figure 1C).
evidence: Supported by gene expression data and citations to Tasic et al., 2016; Tasic et al., 2018

claim: Cluster 3 has a cortical phenotype.
source: Conversely, Cluster 3 was enriched for markers of excitatory cortical populations (e.g., the layer 6b marker Ctgf and the layer 6a marker Sla) (Tasic et al., 2016; Tasic et al., 2018), suggesting a cortical phenotype (Figure 1C).
evidence: Inferred from enrichment of cortical marker genes

claim: Each cluster exhibited enriched expression of many genes associated with neuronal function, suggesting structural and functional heterogeneity between the three clusters.
source: Each cluster also exhibited enriched expression of many other genes associated with neuronal function (Figure 1E), suggesting structural and functional heterogeneity between these three clusters (for full lists of differentially expressed genes, see Supplementary files 1–3).
evidence: Supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 1E

claim: The scRNA-seq dataset largely conformed to three distinct locations within the broader cell-type landscape when incorporating published data.
source: Consistent with the three clusters identified within our dataset, our dataset largely conformed to three distinct locations within the broader cell-type landscape when incorporating published data (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: Supported by integrated analysis with published datasets shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B

claim: Cluster 1 cells occupied an isolated group of Synpr-expressing cells in the integrated dataset.
source: In particular, Cluster 1 cells occupied an isolated group of Synpr-expressing cells, whereas Cluster 2 cells coarsely occupied a distinct location nearby other datasets, but were also enriched for specific marker genes like Nnat (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: Supported by integrated analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2

claim: Cluster 2 cells were enriched for specific marker genes like Nnat.
source: In particular, Cluster 1 cells occupied an isolated group of Synpr-expressing cells, whereas Cluster 2 cells coarsely occupied a distinct location nearby other datasets, but were also enriched for specific marker genes like Nnat (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: Supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C

claim: Nnat-expressing Cluster 2 cells were depleted in Pcp4 expression.
source: In agreement with Cluster 2 being non-cortical, these Nnat-expressing Cluster 2 cells were also depleted in Pcp4 expression (Figure 1—figure supplement 3), a gene strongly expressed in deep cortical layers (but with exception of layer 6 intratelencephalic excitatory neurons: Watakabe et al., 2012; Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: Supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3

claim: Pcp4 is a gene strongly expressed in deep cortical layers (with exception of layer 6 intratelencephalic excitatory neurons).
source: In agreement with Cluster 2 being non-cortical, these Nnat-expressing Cluster 2 cells were also depleted in Pcp4 expression (Figure 1—figure supplement 3), a gene strongly expressed in deep cortical layers (but with exception of layer 6 intratelencephalic excitatory neurons: Watakabe et al., 2012; Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: Supported by citation to Watakabe et al., 2012 and data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4

claim: The scRNA-seq data recapitulates previously described cell types.
source: In collection, this work shows that our scRNA-seq data recapitulates previously described cell types and further suggests new marker genes and specializations that may have been underresolved in previous studies.
evidence: Supported by comparison with published datasets

claim: The scRNA-seq data suggests new marker genes and specializations that may have been underresolved in previous studies.
source: In collection, this work shows that our scRNA-seq data recapitulates previously described cell types and further suggests new marker genes and specializations that may have been underresolved in previous studies.
evidence: Supported by identification of novel marker genes like Slc30a3 and Nnat

claim: Multiplexed fluorescent in situ hybridization allows mapping of 12 RNA targets at single-molecule and single-cell resolution.
source: To do this, we used multiplexed fluorescent in situ hybridization (mFISH) (Wang et al., 2012), allowing us to map 12 RNA targets at a single-molecule and single-cell resolution (Sullivan et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to Wang et al., 2012 and Sullivan et al., 2020

claim: 18,957 excitatory neurons from 5 animals were analyzed using mFISH.
source: We used mFISH to spatially register expression of these 12 genes across anterior, intermediate, and posterior sections of the claustrum (Figure 2A; expansions: Figure 2—figure supplement 2; Video 1; n = 18,957 excitatory neurons from n = 5 animals analyzed).
evidence: Describes the sample size for mFISH analysis

claim: A claustrum population with a relatively central core-like location exhibited expression of Synpr.
source: In doing so, we identified a claustrum population with a relatively central core-like location that exhibited expression of Synpr, and a surrounding shell-like population exhibiting expression of Nnat (Figure 2B–D).
evidence: Supported by mFISH data shown in Figure 2B–D

claim: A surrounding shell-like population exhibited expression of Nnat.
source: In doing so, we identified a claustrum population with a relatively central core-like location that exhibited expression of Synpr, and a surrounding shell-like population exhibiting expression of Nnat (Figure 2B–D).
evidence: Supported by mFISH data shown in Figure 2B–D

claim: The core-shell organization was present across the anterior-posterior axis.
source: This organization was present across the anterior-posterior axis (Figure 2—figure supplement 3) as well as across animals (Figure 2—figure supplement 4), and recapitulated gene-expression properties predicted from scRNA-seq (Figure 2—figure supplement 5).
evidence: Supported by mFISH data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3

claim: The core-shell organization was present across animals.
source: This organization was present across the anterior-posterior axis (Figure 2—figure supplement 3) as well as across animals (Figure 2—figure supplement 4), and recapitulated gene-expression properties predicted from scRNA-seq (Figure 2—figure supplement 5).
evidence: Supported by mFISH data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4

claim: The mFISH data recapitulated gene-expression properties predicted from scRNA-seq.
source: This organization was present across the anterior-posterior axis (Figure 2—figure supplement 3) as well as across animals (Figure 2—figure supplement 4), and recapitulated gene-expression properties predicted from scRNA-seq (Figure 2—figure supplement 5).
evidence: Supported by comparison shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 5

claim: Adjacent to the claustrum populations were other neuronal subtypes enriched for markers of cortical cells, including a cluster with spatial and transcriptional properties of deep layer 6 cells.
source: Adjacent to these populations were other neuronal subtypes enriched for markers of cortical cells, including a cluster with spatial and transcriptional properties of deep layer 6 cells (i.e., a Ctgf-expressing cluster in the deepest cortical layer).
evidence: Supported by mFISH data showing Ctgf expression in deep cortical layers

claim: Claustrum excitatory neuron subtypes are transcriptionally distinct from neighboring cortical neurons.
source: Collectively, these results illustrated that claustrum excitatory neuron subtypes are transcriptionally distinct from neighboring cortical neurons and form a core-shell spatial organization.
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq and mFISH data showing differential gene expression

claim: Claustrum excitatory neuron subtypes form a core-shell spatial organization.
source: Collectively, these results illustrated that claustrum excitatory neuron subtypes are transcriptionally distinct from neighboring cortical neurons and form a core-shell spatial organization.
evidence: Supported by mFISH data showing spatial arrangement of Synpr and Nnat expressing cells

claim: Projections to the RSC and LEC exhibit minimal overlap.
source: To answer this question, we next considered projections to the RSC and LEC, two claustral projections that exhibit minimal overlap (two-color retrograde viral injections: Figure 3A; see also Marriott et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by retrograde tracing data shown in Figure 3A and citation to Marriott et al., 2020

claim: 85% (204/241) of RSC-projecting claustrum cells mapped onto the Synpr-expressing class.
source: Strikingly, 85% (204/241) of RSC-projecting claustrum cells mapped onto the Synpr-expressing class, whereas 84% (238/282) of LEC-projecting claustrum cells mapped onto the Nnat-expressing class (Figure 3C).
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq data with projection labeling shown in Figure 3C

claim: 84% (238/282) of LEC-projecting claustrum cells mapped onto the Nnat-expressing class.
source: Strikingly, 85% (204/241) of RSC-projecting claustrum cells mapped onto the Synpr-expressing class, whereas 84% (238/282) of LEC-projecting claustrum cells mapped onto the Nnat-expressing class (Figure 3C).
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq data with projection labeling shown in Figure 3C

claim: mFISH applied to retrograde-labeled cells provided evidence that Synpr and Nnat were respectively enriched in RSC-projecting and LEC-projecting cells.
source: Similarly, applying mFISH to retrograde-labeled cells provided complementary evidence that Synpr and Nnat were respectively enriched in RSC-projecting and LEC-projecting cells (representative section: Figure 3D–H; all projection cells: Figure 3I, Figure 3—figure supplement 1), and illustrated that RSC- and LEC-projecting cells were enriched in distinct claustral subtypes (216/259 = 83% of RSC-projecting claustral cells were found in core cluster and 276/324 = 85% of LEC-projecting claustral cells were found in shell cluster, n = 4 and n = 2 animals, respectively, Figure 3J).
evidence: Supported by mFISH data with retrograde labeling shown in Figure 3D–I

claim: 83% (216/259) of RSC-projecting claustral cells were found in the core cluster.
source: Similarly, applying mFISH to retrograde-labeled cells provided complementary evidence that Synpr and Nnat were respectively enriched in RSC-projecting and LEC-projecting cells (representative section: Figure 3D–H; all projection cells: Figure 3I, Figure 3—figure supplement 1), and illustrated that RSC- and LEC-projecting cells were enriched in distinct claustral subtypes (216/259 = 83% of RSC-projecting claustral cells were found in core cluster and 276/324 = 85% of LEC-projecting claustral cells were found in shell cluster, n = 4 and n = 2 animals, respectively, Figure 3J).
evidence: Supported by mFISH data with retrograde labeling shown in Figure 3J

claim: 85% (276/324) of LEC-projecting claustral cells were found in the shell cluster.
source: Similarly, applying mFISH to retrograde-labeled cells provided complementary evidence that Synpr and Nnat were respectively enriched in RSC-projecting and LEC-projecting cells (representative section: Figure 3D–H; all projection cells: Figure 3I, Figure 3—figure supplement 1), and illustrated that RSC- and LEC-projecting cells were enriched in distinct claustral subtypes (216/259 = 83% of RSC-projecting claustral cells were found in core cluster and 276/324 = 85% of LEC-projecting claustral cells were found in shell cluster, n = 4 and n = 2 animals, respectively, Figure 3J).
evidence: Supported by mFISH data with retrograde labeling shown in Figure 3J

claim: Distinct excitatory claustrum projection neurons are coherently separable by marker genes, local spatial organization, and long-range projection targets.
source: Thus, distinct excitatory claustrum projection neurons were coherently separable by marker genes, local spatial organization, and long-range projection targets.
evidence: Supported by combined scRNA-seq, mFISH, and retrograde tracing data

claim: Marker-based approaches using individual genes such as Lxn, Gnb4, and Slc17a6 coarsely demarcate the boundaries of the adult mouse claustrum.
source: Marker-based approaches using individual genes such as Lxn, Gnb4, and Slc17a6 coarsely demarcate the boundaries of the adult mouse claustrum (Fodoulian et al., 2020; Kitanishi and Matsuo, 2017; Mathur et al., 2009; Peng et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2017; Watakabe et al., 2012), but it is unclear if these different genes all converge upon a monolithic cellular population or embody different claustrum subtypes (and potentially include phenotypically cortical cells: Bruguier et al., 2020; Molnár et al., 2020; Puelles et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple studies

claim: It is unclear if different marker genes all converge upon a monolithic cellular population or embody different claustrum subtypes.
source: Marker-based approaches using individual genes such as Lxn, Gnb4, and Slc17a6 coarsely demarcate the boundaries of the adult mouse claustrum (Fodoulian et al., 2020; Kitanishi and Matsuo, 2017; Mathur et al., 2009; Peng et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2017; Watakabe et al., 2012), but it is unclear if these different genes all converge upon a monolithic cellular population or embody different claustrum subtypes (and potentially include phenotypically cortical cells: Bruguier et al., 2020; Molnár et al., 2020; Puelles et al., 2016).
evidence: Represents a gap in knowledge addressed by this study

claim: Retrograde tracing from the cortex has been useful for identifying claustrum projection neurons.
source: Retrograde tracing from the cortex has been useful for identifying claustrum projection neurons (Marriott et al., 2020; Minciacchi et al., 1985; Watson et al., 2017; Zingg et al., 2018), but similarly it remains unknown whether projection-labeled claustrum cells are intrinsically homogeneous.
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple studies

claim: It remains unknown whether projection-labeled claustrum cells are intrinsically homogeneous.
source: Retrograde tracing from the cortex has been useful for identifying claustrum projection neurons (Marriott et al., 2020; Minciacchi et al., 1985; Watson et al., 2017; Zingg et al., 2018), but similarly it remains unknown whether projection-labeled claustrum cells are intrinsically homogeneous.
evidence: Represents a gap in knowledge addressed by this study

claim: The approach integrating transcriptomic and circuit-level approaches identified two claustrum cell subtypes that are molecularly distinguishable from surrounding cortex.
source: Our approach here, integrating transcriptomic and circuit-level approaches, identified two claustrum cell subtypes that are molecularly distinguishable from surrounding cortex (Figures 1 and 2) and associated with different long-range projection patterns (Figure 3).
evidence: Supported by data presented in Figures 1, 2, and 3

claim: The two claustrum cell subtypes are associated with different long-range projection patterns.
source: Our approach here, integrating transcriptomic and circuit-level approaches, identified two claustrum cell subtypes that are molecularly distinguishable from surrounding cortex (Figures 1 and 2) and associated with different long-range projection patterns (Figure 3).
evidence: Supported by data presented in Figure 3

claim: The RSC and LEC reflect the two most spatially distinct core vs. shell projections.
source: In previous projection mapping, it has been shown that the RSC and LEC reflect the two most spatially distinct core vs. shell projections (Marriott et al., 2020), and thus it is likely that other claustral projections comprise more of a mosaicism of core and shell transcriptomic phenotypes.
evidence: Supported by citation to Marriott et al., 2020

claim: Other claustral projections likely comprise more of a mosaicism of core and shell transcriptomic phenotypes.
source: In previous projection mapping, it has been shown that the RSC and LEC reflect the two most spatially distinct core vs. shell projections (Marriott et al., 2020), and thus it is likely that other claustral projections comprise more of a mosaicism of core and shell transcriptomic phenotypes.
evidence: Inferred from the finding that RSC and LEC are the most distinct projections

claim: The claustral organizational scheme involves discretely separate transcriptomic subtypes that are biased – but not wholly separable – according to long-range projection targets.
source: Ultimately, this suggests a claustral organizational scheme wherein discretely separate transcriptomic subtypes are biased – but not wholly separable – according to long-range projection targets (Cembrowski and Menon, 2018a).
evidence: Inferred from the data showing 83-85% correspondence between subtypes and projections

claim: The relationship between the claustrum and the nearby deep insular cortex and dorsal endopiriform cortex is often debated.
source: As the relationship between the claustrum and the nearby deep insular cortex and dorsal endopiriform cortex is often debated (Bruguier et al., 2020; Marriott et al., 2020; Mathur, 2014; Mathur et al., 2009; Smith et al., 2019; Watakabe et al., 2012; Watson et al., 2017; Zingg et al., 2020), it is important to discuss our work in the context of these adjacent regions.
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple studies

claim: Relative to the deep insular cortex, the work shows a general lack of deep cortical markers for two distinct neuron types.
source: Relative to the deep insular cortex, our work here shows a general lack of deep cortical markers for two distinct neuron types, as well as enrichment of genes in these types that are not typically associated with deep cortex (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplements 3 and 4).
evidence: Supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 1C and supplements

claim: The two neuron types show enrichment of genes that are not typically associated with deep cortex.
source: Relative to the deep insular cortex, our work here shows a general lack of deep cortical markers for two distinct neuron types, as well as enrichment of genes in these types that are not typically associated with deep cortex (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplements 3 and 4).
evidence: Supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 1C and supplements

claim: Both neuron types show enrichment of some claustrum marker genes relative to cortical neurons (e.g., Gnb4).
source: In conjunction with both of these neuron types showing enrichment of some claustrum marker genes relative to cortical neurons (e.g., Gnb4: Figure 1C), we interpret these transcriptomic cell types as claustrum core and shell neuron subtypes.
evidence: Supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 1C

claim: The transcriptomic cell types are interpreted as claustrum core and shell neuron subtypes.
source: In conjunction with both of these neuron types showing enrichment of some claustrum marker genes relative to cortical neurons (e.g., Gnb4: Figure 1C), we interpret these transcriptomic cell types as claustrum core and shell neuron subtypes.
evidence: Inferred from the combination of marker gene expression and spatial location

claim: The scRNA-seq and smFISH validation focused on the atlas-defined spatial extent of the claustrum.
source: Relative to the dorsal endopiriform cortex, our scRNA-seq and smFISH validation focused on the atlas-defined spatial extent of the claustrum; thus, future work targeting the dorsal endopiriform cortex will be needed to examine the transcriptomic relationship between these two regions.
evidence: Describes the spatial scope of the study

claim: Future work targeting the dorsal endopiriform cortex will be needed to examine the transcriptomic relationship between the claustrum and dorsal endopiriform cortex.
source: Relative to the dorsal endopiriform cortex, our scRNA-seq and smFISH validation focused on the atlas-defined spatial extent of the claustrum; thus, future work targeting the dorsal endopiriform cortex will be needed to examine the transcriptomic relationship between these two regions.
evidence: Represents a limitation and future direction

claim: The findings will allow subtype-specific claustral function to be assayed in future experiments by leveraging either marker genes or projection pathways.
source: Collectively, our results will allow subtype-specific claustral function to be assayed in future experiments by leveraging either marker genes or projection pathways (Cembrowski, 2019).
evidence: Represents a potential application of the findings

claim: The findings will help to guide and inform observational and interventional experiments, and bridge claustrum cell-type identity, structure, and function.
source: Thus, our findings here will help to guide and inform observational and interventional experiments, and bridge claustrum cell-type identity, structure, and function.
evidence: Represents a potential application of the findings

claim: The scRNA-seq data has been hosted online in conjunction with analysis and visualization tools at http://scrnaseq.janelia.org/claustrum.
source: To facilitate such experiments and interpretations, we have hosted our scRNA-seq data online in conjunction with analysis and visualization tools (http://scrnaseq.janelia.org/claustrum).
evidence: Describes data availability

claim: The web portal will help to identify how specific genes, cells, and circuits mechanistically drive claustral function and behavior.
source: This web portal will help to identify how specific genes, cells, and circuits mechanistically drive claustral function and behavior.
evidence: Represents a potential application of the resource

claim: All procedures were approved by the University of British Columbia Animal Care Committee (protocol A18-0267).
source: All procedures were approved by the University of British Columbia Animal Care Committee (protocol A18-0267), the University of Alberta Health Science Laboratory Animal Services Animal Care and Use Committee (protocol AUP2711), and the Janelia Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (protocol 17-159).
evidence: Describes ethical approval

claim: All procedures were approved by the University of Alberta Health Science Laboratory Animal Services Animal Care and Use Committee (protocol AUP2711).
source: All procedures were approved by the University of British Columbia Animal Care Committee (protocol A18-0267), the University of Alberta Health Science Laboratory Animal Services Animal Care and Use Committee (protocol AUP2711), and the Janelia Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (protocol 17-159).
evidence: Describes ethical approval

claim: All procedures were approved by the Janelia Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (protocol 17-159).
source: All procedures were approved by the University of British Columbia Animal Care Committee (protocol A18-0267), the University of Alberta Health Science Laboratory Animal Services Animal Care and Use Committee (protocol AUP2711), and the Janelia Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (protocol 17-159).
evidence: Describes ethical approval

claim: Mature C57BL/6 mice of either sex were used for retrograde tracer injections.
source: Mature C57BL/6 mice of either sex were used for injections, and randomly assigned retrograde injection locations and tracers.
evidence: Describes experimental subjects

claim: Mice were randomly assigned retrograde injection locations and tracers.
source: Mature C57BL/6 mice of either sex were used for injections, and randomly assigned retrograde injection locations and tracers.
evidence: Describes experimental design

claim: 200 nL of retrograde tracer was injected for all retrograde tracing experiments.
source: All injections were made using pressure injection, with 200 nL of retrograde tracer (Tervo et al., 2016) being injected.
evidence: Describes experimental procedure

claim: Manual capture approach was used to harvest cells from 4 mature male C57BL/6 mice for scRNA-seq.
source: We used a manual capture approach to harvest cells from n = 4 mature male C57BL/6 mice.
evidence: Describes experimental procedure

claim: Fluorescent tracers were used to delineate and grossly microdissect the claustrum from horizontal sections.
source: To facilitate microdissection of the claustrum, fluorescent tracers were used to delineate and grossly microdissect the claustrum from horizontal sections.
evidence: Describes experimental procedure

claim: In one animal, retrograde rAAV2-retro-CAG-GFP was injected into the anterior cingulate cortex to facilitate gross microdissection of the claustrum.
source: In one animal, retrograde rAAV2-retro-CAG-GFP (Tervo et al., 2016) was injected into the anterior cingulate cortex to facilitate gross microdissection of the claustrum (Jackson et al., 2018), but not used to select for individual cells (i.e., GFP expression was used to microdissect the claustrum but cells were picked blind relative to GFP expression).
evidence: Describes experimental procedure

claim: In one animal, cells from separate anterior and posterior sections were obtained, allowing analysis of potential anterior vs. posterior differences in claustrum gene expression.
source: In this animal, cells from separate anterior and posterior sections were obtained, allowing analysis of potential anterior vs. posterior differences in claustrum gene expression (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Describes experimental design

claim: For three mice, green and red retrobeads were respectively injected into the LEC and RSC.
source: To build the projection-specific dataset, for the remaining three mice, green and red retrobeads were respectively injected into the LEC and RSC, with this labeling used for gross microdissection as well as to select a subset of projection-specific cells for RNA-seq.
evidence: Describes experimental procedure

claim: Manual purification was used to capture cells in capillary needles in approximately 0.1–0.5 mL ACSF cocktail.
source: In all cases, manual purification (Hempel et al., 2007) was used to capture cells in capillary needles in approximately 0.1–0.5 mL ACSF cocktail, placed into 8-well strips containing 3 µL of cell collection buffer (0.1% Triton X-100, 0.2 U/µL RNAse inhibitor; Lucigen, Middleton, WI), and generally processed according to published methodology (Cembrowski et al., 2018b; Schretter et al., 2020).
evidence: Describes experimental procedure with citations
